why: Doc sentence is verbatim (changelog.md:207, Update 2.1.212, July 17 2026); the whole line is one bullet and the trailing clause ('/clear resets the budget') does not reverse it. The companion concurrent cap is also verbatim at changelog.md:101 (default 20, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS). The grep for CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS really does return 0 hits, and the cited packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:604 really does read 'concurrency: cfg.concurrency ?? DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY'. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and the finding stopped exactly one line short: spawner.ts:603 is 'fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100'. That budget IS the per-session total-spawn cap. It is enforced at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 as 'if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error("child-session-fanout-limit")' — against children.length, the parent's FULL record list, not the active subset computed one line earlier at :147. That list is append-only (the sole removal, :154, is the cancelled-start rollback), so a finished child still counts: this is a cumulative lifetime cap on spawns per parent session, exactly the documented semantic. Proven by packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.test.ts:174-184 — child-1 is stopped (twice) and then starting child-3 with 'fanout: 1, concurrency: 2' still throws 'child-session-fanout-limit'. So the claim's core assertion, 'a semaphore throttles simultaneity but never caps total spawns, so a session can spawn unboundedly many subagents in sequence', is refuted by a passing test. The second cap is also present and also missed: child-session-service.ts:149 'if (active.length >= input.budgets.concurrency) throw new Error("child-session-concurrency-limit")' is a per-parent CONCURRENT-subagent cap enforced on the host, in addition to (not the same as) the process-wide DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY semaphore the finding described. Shipped defaults come from DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:102-112): maxAgents 1000, concurrency 16, wired maxAgents -> maxFanout -> budgets.fanout at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280; packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49 documents maxAgents as the 'Runaway backstop: maximum agent() calls per workflow run'. SessionManager narrows further on specific paths (fanout: min(parentBudgets?.fanout ?? 1, 1) for hook-effect children at SessionManager.ts:4933; fanout: 1 for the judge at :11217; min-with-inherited at :11142). Finally, the absent identifiers are the expected shape of this fork, not a gap: Nessy is renamed throughout (NESSY_ prefixes, @nessy-agent scope, Pi orchestrator), so CLAUDE_CODE_* env names would not exist even where the behaviour matches — a textbook 'identically-named symbol in a sibling subsystem' inversion. Nothing in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 covers this; the refutation is on evidence, not on a recorded decision.
correctedState: Both caps exist under Pi/Nessy names, and both are enforced on the host, not in the spawner. Per-session TOTAL subagent-spawn cap: budgets.fanout, enforced cumulatively at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 against the parent's append-only child-record list (terminated children still count; regression test at child-session-service.test.ts:180-184). CONCURRENT-subagent cap: budgets.concurrency, enforced at child-session-service.ts:149 against starting|running children only, on top of the process-wide semaphore. Shipped defaults: maxAgents 1000 and concurrency 16 (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:102-112), plumbed via configureSpawner({ maxFanout: config.orchestrator?.maxAgents, concurrency: config.orchestrator?.concurrency }) at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1277-1280; the spawner's own fallbacks when no host config arrives are 100 and 16 (spawner.ts:603-604). The only genuine deltas are cosmetic/numeric and were not what the finding claimed: our defaults are 1000/16 against Claude's 200/20, the knobs are orchestrator config keys (orchestrator.maxAgents, orchestrator.concurrency) rather than CLAUDE_CODE_* environment overrides, and whether a conversation clear resets the accumulated fanout budget was not verified either way.
